source: Terms used in the Build Your First Systems Diagram deck (U1 Block 2b). Definitions match the U1 EAL pre-teach table and the Four Spheres reading.
translationStatus: English only. The language selector stays off this deck until the U1 vocabulary translations are verified.

terms.plain: The air: the layer of gases around the planet.
terms.note: From AISC: the monsoon clouds, the humidity you walk into at 3 pm.

terms.plain: All the water on Earth, in every form: oceans, rivers, ice, groundwater, water vapor.
terms.note: From AISC: the Bay of Bengal, the water tanker, the Adyar river.

terms.plain: The rock: crust, mantle, core, and the soil and sand made from them.
terms.note: From AISC: Marina Beach sand, the red laterite soil in the garden.

terms.plain: All living things, and what they make.
terms.note: From AISC: the crows, the neem trees, you.

terms.plain: A drawing of parts as labeled circles and the ways they affect each other as arrows with verbs on them.
terms.note: Two circles and one arrow with a verb is already a systems diagram. Everything after that is the same drawing, extended.

terms.plain: Two or more arrows that go round and come back to where they started, so a change in one part comes back to affect that same part.
terms.note: A loop gets a sign, + or −. A cycle (water, carbon, oxygen) does not.

terms.plain: A loop where a push comes back bigger, so the change grows.
terms.note: Positive is a direction, not a judgment. Melting ice exposing dark ocean that melts more ice is positive, and not good.

terms.plain: A loop where a push comes back smaller, so the change is damped and the system settles.
terms.note: The rock thermostat is the classic example: warmer air, more weathering, less carbon dioxide, cooler air.
